questions.text: Which decommissioned Indian Naval Ship’s (INS) artefacts and weapon systems are primarily showcased at the ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’ inaugurated in Lucknow in May 2026?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is INS Gomati

In News

  • On May 30, 2026, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath jointly inaugurated the ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’ in Lucknow.

Key Points

  • INS Gomati: The museum is built to honour the spirit and prowess of the Indian Navy by showcasing artefacts from INS Gomati, which was decommissioned on May 29, 2022, after 34 years of service.
  • Displayed Artefacts: The park features the AK 726 Naval Gun, ZIF 101 launcher for Surface-to-Air Missiles, and a walkthrough museum of the TU 142M maritime patrol aircraft.
  • Cost and Area: The Open-Air Display Museum was built at a cost of Rs 19 crore and spans over an area of two acres.
  • Strategic Significance: The museum aims to inspire the youth and serves as a symbol of the Navy's operational readiness, including its role in Operation Sindoor where its posture confined the Pakistan Navy to its ports.

Additional Information

  • INS Gomati History: Named after the river Gomti, it was the third ship of the Godavari class guided-missile frigates and was commissioned on April 16, 1988.
  • Service Record: It participated in Operations Cactus, Parakram, and Rainbow and was twice awarded the Unit Citation (2007-08 and 2019-20).
  • Aatmanirbhar Bharat: The event highlighted initiatives like iDEX and ADITI, aiming for complete self-reliance in the defence sector.

Important Points

  • Defence Production: Domestic production increased from Rs 46,000 crore in 2014 to over Rs 1.51 lakh crore currently.
  • Defence Exports: Exports have grown from less than Rs 1,000 crore in 2014 to approximately Rs 40,000 crore.
  • UP Defence Industrial Corridor: The state is playing a pivotal role in strengthening India's defence manufacturing ecosystem.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as India's Executive Director at the World Bank for a tenure of three years?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Neelkanth Mishra

In News

  • Economist Neelkanth Mishra has been appointed as India's Executive Director at the World Bank.

Key Points

  • Neelkanth Mishra: He has been appointed for a three-year tenure at the World Bank headquarters in Washington, DC.
  • Parameswaran Iyer: Mishra will succeed Parameswaran Iyer, whose tenure has been extended until the former assumes office.
  • Dhanendra Kumar: Mentioned in the news as the 1st chairman of CCI who passed away, and is not related to the current appointment.
  • Ravi Hari: He is the author who published the report and is not an appointee to any financial institution.
  • The appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC).

Additional Information

  • The Executive Director represents India at the World Bank's Board.
  • The role involves overseeing lending operations, development projects, financial policies, and governance decisions.
  • The position is considered a vital economic diplomacy role for shaping global development financing and poverty reduction initiatives.

Important Points

  • The appointment comes at a time when India is seeking a stronger voice in international financial institutions.
  • The World Bank headquarters is located in Washington, DC.
  • The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) is the body responsible for finalizing this high-level international representation.

questions.text: Suman Kalyanpur, whose demise was condoled by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in June 2026, was a legendary figure in which of the following fields?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Singing

In News

  • Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed deep grief over the passing of the popular singer, Smt. Suman Kalyanpur, on June 1, 2026.

Key Points

  • Suman Kalyanpur was a renowned popular singer whose melodious voice and soulful renditions significantly enriched India’s cultural world.
  • Through her extensive work, she created a special place among music lovers and admirers of Indian cinema.
  • The Prime Minister noted that her contributions to the music industry were vital to the country's cultural heritage.
  • Options like Sports, Literature, and Politics are incorrect as the official release explicitly identifies her as a singer.

Additional Information

  • The condolence message was shared by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) and posted on the Prime Minister's official X (formerly Twitter) handle.
  • The news release was disseminated by PIB Delhi and made available in several regional languages including Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, Gujarati, and Tamil.

Important Points

  • The event occurred on June 1, 2026, marking the loss of a prominent voice in the Indian music and cinema industry.

questions.text: Who was named the Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the SAFF Women’s Championship 2026?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Sanfida Nongrum

In News

  • The Indian women’s football team reclaimed the SAFF Women’s Championship crown by defeating Bangladesh 3-1 in the 2026 final held in Goa.

Key Points

  • Sanfida Nongrum was awarded the title of Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the tournament.
  • She played a crucial role in the final, scoring India's second goal in the 46th minute to regain the lead.
  • Prior to the final, she also scored the winning goal for India in the semi-finals against Bhutan.
  • In the final match against Bangladesh, her positioning and offensive play kept constant pressure on the defenders, helping India secure the 3-1 victory.

Additional Information

  • Aveka Singh finished as the competition’s top scorer with a total of four goals.
  • Panthoi Chanu Elangbam received the Best Goalkeeper award for her performance throughout the tournament.
  • Nepal was honored with the Fair Play award.
  • The final took place at the Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Margao, Goa.

Important Points

  • This victory marked India's sixth SAFF Women’s Championship title, a record-extending achievement in the history of the competition.
  • India reclaimed the title after a gap of seven years, with their last win occurring in 2019.
  • During the 2026 edition, India remained dominant by scoring 18 goals in four matches and conceded only one goal, which was in the final.

questions.text: What is the name of the coordinated anti-narcotics operation recently carried out by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) in Kerala to seize over 24 kg of narcotic drugs?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Operation Chakravyuh

In News

  • The Cochin Unit of the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intensified its anti-narcotics drive in Kerala under Operation Chakravyuh.

Key Points

  • Operation Chakravyuh: It is the specific name of the coordinated operation conducted by the DRI to dismantle drug trafficking networks in Kerala.
  • Seizure Details: Over 24 kg of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances, including methaqualone, methamphetamine, and hashish oil, were seized at Kochi, Malappuram, and Thiruvananthapuram.
  • Arrests: Five individuals were apprehended under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985 during these operations.
  • Smuggling Modes: The contraband was detected in passenger baggage at the airport, courier consignments, and outbound export cargo.

Additional Information

  • In the last financial year, the DRI's Cochin Zonal Unit seized narcotics valued at Rs. 70.76 crore in Kerala and arrested 21 persons.
  • The DRI's efforts align with the Government of India's vision of "Nasha Mukt Bharat" (Drug-Free India).

Important Points

  • The operation targeted both international and domestic trafficking channels to safeguard society from narcotic menaces.
  • The NDPS Act, 1985 serves as the legal framework for the apprehension and prosecution of individuals involved in drug trafficking in India.

questions.text: According to the tribute paid by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Bhagwan Birsa Munda fought against foreign rule for the protection of which of the following core elements?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Water, Forest, and Land

In News

  • Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi paid tributes to Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda Ji on his martyrdom day on June 9, 2026.

Key Points

  • The Prime Minister highlighted that Bhagwan Birsa Munda fought with indomitable courage against foreign rule specifically for the protection of water, forest, and land (Jal, Jangal, Zameen).
  • His entire life was dedicated to the tribal community, focusing on the protection of their self-respect, culture, and rights.
  • The term "Dharti Aaba" is used to refer to Bhagwan Birsa Munda, signifying his deep connection to the earth and his community.
  • The other options like Education, Healthcare, Trade, or Infrastructure are not mentioned in the official tribute as the core focus of his struggle against the foreign rule.

Additional Information

  • The tribute was posted on June 9, 2026, which marks the sacrifice day of the tribal leader.
  • The message emphasized that his legacy of sacrificing everything for the motherland continues to inspire patriotism across generations in India.

Important Points

  • Bhagwan Birsa Munda is a legendary figure in Indian history known for leading a tribal religious millenarian movement during the late 19th century.
  • His struggle was centered around the preservation of tribal resources and resisting British colonial expansionism.

questions.text: According to the commemorative book released by Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh in May 2026, India compelled Pakistan to seek a ceasefire within how many days during Operation Sindoor?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Four days

In News

  • On May 29, 2026, Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh released a commemorative volume on Operation Sindoor in New Delhi.

Key Points

  • Operation Sindoor is described as an unprecedented success in Indian military history where the Indian forces compelled Pakistan to seek a ceasefire within just four days.
  • The commemorative book documents the personal testimonies of 100 officers, sailors, airmen, and other soldiers who participated in the operation.
  • Unlike traditional military historiography that focuses on decisions made at headquarters, this volume captures the texture of war as lived by ground-level personnel like pilots, sailors at action stations, and special forces operators.
  • The Raksha Mantri highlighted that the operation was different from all other wars India has fought, emphasizing the human dimension of modern warfare where leadership and courage translate strategy into success.

Additional Information

  • The book was released in the presence of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan, and the three service chiefs: Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi (Navy), General Upendra Dwivedi (Army), and Air Chief Marshal AP Singh (Air Force).
  • The volume was compiled under the guidance of the Chief of Defence Staff with publication support provided by the United Service Institution of India (USI).
  • Contributions were made by the Additional Directorate General of Strategic Communication and the Directorate of Media and Public Relations.

Important Points

  • The publication spans accounts across the three Services and the Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff.
  • It includes perspectives from combat aviators, naval watchkeepers, surface-to-air missile crews, and medical officers, aiming to recover the lived experience of the conflict.

questions.text:
Consider the following pairs of Foreign Higher Education Institutions (FHEIs) and the Indian cities where they have been approved to establish campuses as per the Letters of Approval (LoA) issued in June 2026:
1. University of Bristol : Bengaluru
2. University of York : Mumbai
3. University of New South Wales : Bengaluru
How many of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Two only

In News

  • The Ministry of Education issued Letters of Approval (LoA) to the University of Bristol, University of York, and University of New South Wales (UNSW) to set up campuses in India.

Key Points

  • Pair 1 is incorrectly matched: The University of Bristol is set to establish its Mumbai Enterprise Campus, focusing on areas like Data Science, Finance, and Entrepreneurship.
  • Pair 2 is correctly matched: The University of York will establish its first overseas campus in Mumbai, offering programmes in Cyber Security, AI, and Creative Industries.
  • Pair 3 is correctly matched: The University of New South Wales (UNSW) will establish UNSW Bengaluru at Manyata Business Park, scheduled to open from August 2026.
  • Hence, only two pairs (Pair 2 and Pair 3) are correctly matched.

Additional Information

  • With these new approvals, a total of five LoAs have been issued under the UGC Regulations for Foreign Higher Educational Institutions, including the University of Southampton and University of Liverpool.
  • The University of Southampton has already commenced its academic operations starting from the 2025–26 session.
  • The UGC has also issued 10 Letters of Intent (LoIs) to other institutions from the UK, US, Australia, and Italy.

Important Points

  • This initiative is a major step towards fulfilling the internationalisation vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.
  • Institutions like Deakin University, University of Wollongong, and Queen’s University Belfast have already started operations in GIFT City.
  • The new campuses in Mumbai and Bengaluru aim to strengthen India's knowledge and innovation hotspots through global partnerships.

questions.text: Which nodal laboratory of the Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) was primarily responsible for the indigenous development of the RudraM-II Air-to-Surface Missile?

options.text: Combat Vehicles Research and Development Establishment (CVRDE)

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad

In News

  • The Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Indian Air Force (IAF) successfully conducted flight-tests of the RudraM-II Air-to-Surface Missile from an airborne platform.

Key Points

  • The RudraM-II has been indigenously developed by the Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad, serving as the nodal DRDO laboratory for this project.
  • The development was carried out in collaboration with sister laboratories, including the Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL), High Energy Materials Research Laboratory (HEMRL), and Armament Research & Development Establishment (ARDE).
  • The missile tests were conducted under extreme release conditions, and it successfully hit a predefined target with pin-point accuracy.
  • Flight data for the mission was captured by range instruments at the Integrated Test Range (ITR), Chandipur.

Additional Information

  • Significant contributions were made by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), Regional Centre for Military Airworthiness, and the Missile System Quality Assurance Agency.
  • Development cum Production Partners (DcPPs) and various private industries also played a crucial role in the missile's development and testing.

Important Points

  • The successful test demonstrates the maturity of indigenous defence technologies and supports the Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance) initiative in advanced weapon systems.
  • The RudraM-II is an Air-to-Surface Missile, a critical component for the Indian Air Force's offensive capabilities.

questions.text: In May 2026, which Indian Air Force strategic airlift aircraft was utilized to transport the sacred relics of Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana to Mongolia?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is IL-76 Gajraj

In News

  • The Indian Air Force (IAF) airlifted the sacred Buddhist relics of Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana to Mongolia in May 2026.

Key Points

  • On 30 May 2026, an Indian Air Force IL-76 strategic airlift aircraft, known as Gajraj, transported the relics from Delhi to Mongolia.
  • The aircraft undertook an overnight flight and landed in Mongolia at 1125 hrs IST.
  • This mission was conducted to support India's efforts to strengthen cultural ties with friendly nations.
  • The use of the IL-76 Gajraj reflects the IAF's capability to support national objectives and global cultural outreach. Hence, option 2 is the correct answer.

Additional Information

  • The relics belong to Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana, who were the chief disciples of Gautama Buddha.
  • The mission highlights the intersection of military logistics and cultural diplomacy.

Important Points

  • The IL-76 is a heavy-duty strategic aircraft used by the IAF for large-scale transport operations.
  • The initiative aligns with India's broader Act East policy and cultural engagement with Buddhist nations.

questions.text: Which initiative was awarded the 2026 Food Planet Prize, the world’s largest environmental award for food systems, receiving a prize of USD 1.5 million?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is AP Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF)

In News

  • The AP Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF) programme has won the prestigious 2026 Food Planet Prize for its nature-positive global farming model.

Key Points

  • The Food Planet Prize is considered the world’s largest environmental award focused on transforming global food systems.
  • The award, worth USD 1.5 million (approximately Rs 14 crore), was presented by the Curt Bergfors Foundation on June 2 in Båstad, Sweden.
  • APCNF emerged as the winner among four global finalists. The other three finalists—Conscious Kitchen (US), NoPalm Ingredients (Netherlands), and Savanna Institute (US)—received USD 150,000 each.
  • The jury praised APCNF for its nature-positive model, which has helped 1.8 million farmers in 8,000 villages adopt natural farming over the last decade.

Additional Information

  • Executive Vice Chairman T Vijay Kumar attributed the success to women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and rural communities.
  • Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu hailed the award as a first for India.
  • The programme is recognized as one of the world’s largest agroecology movements.

Important Points

  • The Andhra Pradesh government has pledged to make the state a 100% natural farming State by 2047.
  • The Food Planet Prize recognition reflects the alignment of government policy, scientific knowledge, and community institutions.

questions.text:
Which of the following players were among the award winners in the 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL)?

1. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
2. Kagiso Rabada
3. Sai Sudharsan
4. Mohammed Siraj

Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 1, 2, 3 and 4

In News

  • The 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL) concluded on May 31, 2026, with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) winning the title for the second consecutive year.

Key Points

  • Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (Rajasthan Royals): He secured multiple awards including the Orange Cap (776 runs), Most Valuable Player (MVP) (436.5 points), and Emerging Player award. He also won Super Striker and Super Sixes awards.
  • Kagiso Rabada (Gujarat Titans): He was the recipient of the Purple Cap for taking the most wickets (29 wickets) in the season.
  • Sai Sudharsan (Gujarat Titans): He won the award for hitting the Most Fours in the 2026 season, totaling 75 fours.
  • Mohammed Siraj (Gujarat Titans): He received the Green Dot Ball Award for bowling 172 dot balls during the tournament.
  • Since all four players listed in the question received individual awards, the correct code is 1, 2, 3 and 4.

Additional Information

  • Manish Pandey (RCB) won the Catch of the Season for his one-handed catch to dismiss Tim David.
  • Punjab Kings received the Fair Play Award for their exemplary conduct on the field.
  • The Cricket Association of Bengal won the Pitch & Ground award for venues hosting 5+ matches, while the Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association won for venues hosting fewer than 4 matches.

Important Points

  • Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) defeated Gujarat Titans (GT) by 5 wickets in the final held at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad.
  • Virat Kohli was named the Player of the Match in the final.
  • Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made history as the youngest player to win the Orange Cap (15 years old) and the first to achieve the MVP + Emerging Player double in a single season.

questions.text: As of June 2026, how many Credit-linked Central Government Schemes are integrated into the Jan Samarth Portal for application submissions?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 16

In News

  • The Jan Samarth Portal marked 4 years of its journey on 6 June 2022, facilitating digital financial inclusion and seamless credit delivery across India.

Key Points

  • The Jan Samarth Portal serves as a unified digital gateway that streamlines the credit application process for 16 Credit-linked Central Government Schemes.
  • These 16 schemes cover various categories including Agriculture, Livelihood, Education, Housing, and Business Activity.
  • The portal was designed to reduce procedural complexities and directly connect lenders with beneficiaries, ensuring a more transparent and efficient credit delivery system.
  • By integrating these 16 schemes, the portal allows users to check eligibility for multiple schemes simultaneously by answering a few basic questions.

Additional Information

  • The portal is available in 8 different languages: English, Hindi, Gujarati, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali, and Kannada.
  • As of 01 June 2026, approximately 54.10 lakh applications amounting to ₹ 3,00,951 crore have been processed through the portal.
  • The platform has onboarded 269 Member Lending Institutions, including 12 Public Sector Banks, 20 Private Sector Banks, and 180 District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs).

Important Points

  • The portal provides an end-to-end digital lending process, offering in-principle sanctions and real-time updates to beneficiaries.
  • It is integrated with key government databases like UIDAI (Aadhaar), UDYAM, GST, and CBDT for faster loan processing and verification.
  • The portal is accessible 24x7 via its official website and mobile applications for both Android and iOS.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone and the new Indian Railways logo:

1) The South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone comprises divisions that cover the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
2) The revised Indian Railways logo, approved for official use in May 2026, incorporates 18 stars in blue colour.
3) The foundation stone for the SCoR headquarters was laid at Mudasarlova in Visakhapatnam in January 2025.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 3

In News

  • Indian Railways has unveiled a new 18-star logo following the creation of the South Coast Railway (SCoR) Zone, which became operational on June 1, 2026.

Key Points

  • Statement 1 is correct: The South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone comprises Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada, and Visakhapatnam divisions, covering the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: The revised Indian Railways logo incorporates 18 stars in red colour (not blue), consequent upon the creation of SCoR as the 18th Zonal Railway.
  • Statement 3 is correct: On January 8, 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone for the SCoR Zone headquarters at Mudasarlova in Visakhapatnam.

Additional Information

  • The new headquarters in Visakhapatnam is being developed on 52.2 acres of land at an estimated cost of Rs 183.58 crore.
  • The Waltair Division of East Coast Railway was bifurcated; one part became the Visakhapatnam Division under SCoR, while the other was renamed the Rayagada Division under East Coast Railway.

Important Points

  • The South Coast Railway (SCoR) is the 18th zonal railway of India.
  • The logo was approved by the Chairman of the Railway Board (CRB) & CEO for official use across Indian Railways on May 27, 2026.
